chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Barqi (may God have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Yaqub ibn Salim, who linked the hadith to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) in a lengthy hadith said: 'Three people should not ride on a single animal together; if they do, the one who is sitting ahead is cursed.'

key_terms.الْمُقَدَّمُ: the one in front / the leader
key_terms.يَرْتَدِفُ: to ride behind one another / to share a mount

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on three people riding one animal together in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Khisal* highlights the etiquette of travel and social hierarchy, identifying the front rider as the one bearing the primary burden or leading the group, thus incurring a curse for potential arrogance or neglect. It reflects the Shia emphasis on modesty and the spiritual dangers of assuming a position of superiority without due humility. The ruling serves as a practical reminder to maintain balance and avoid the pitfalls of status in communal activities.
